paraphrase: Inner aim with outer gaze, free of blinking — this is the śāmbhavī seal, hidden in all the tantras.
notes: Ref: only v. 1 is numbered in the e-text; other passages are cited by e-text page (p.1–p.4).
speaker: Maheśvara

original.text: अन्तर्लक्ष्यं त्वहिर्दृष्टिर्निमेषोन्मेष वर्जितम् । इयं सा शाम्भवी मुद्रा सर्वन्तेषु गोपिता
original.licence: e-text quoted with attribution; licence as for the source file

paraphrase: See within the body the consciousness (citi) that witnesses the rise and fall of all beings, full, dense with bliss, immortal; if Śiva is in one place, the mind in another, Śakti in another and the breath in another, there is no success even in hundreds of crores of aeons.
notes: Ref: only v. 1 is numbered in the e-text; other passages are cited by e-text page (p.1–p.4).
speaker: Maheśvara

paraphrase: How can there be knowledge while the mind lives, and the mind does not die while the breath lives; when both breath and mind dissolve, a man attains liberation, not otherwise. Until the moving breath enters the middle path, until the bindu is firm, until the natural (sahaja) state arises, all talk of knowledge is hypocritical prattle.
notes: Ref: only v. 1 is numbered in the e-text; other passages are cited by e-text page (p.1–p.4). The second verse is the same as HYP 4.114.
speaker: Maheśvara

paraphrase: 'New moon', 'first day' and 'full moon' are the closed eye, the opened eye and the half-open gaze; 'desire' (kāma) is longing for objects and 'poison' (viṣa) its dissolution — abandoning both, one should resort to the spotless (nirañjana); placing the mind in the midst of Śakti and Śakti in the midst of mind, seeing the mind by the mind, one should contemplate the supreme state.
notes: Ref: only v. 1 is numbered in the e-text; other passages are cited by e-text page (p.1–p.4).
speaker: Maheśvara (answering Matsyendra)

paraphrase: The mind alone is the seed, the cause of arising and persistence; from the mind bindu arises, as ghee from milk.
notes: Ref: only v. 1 is numbered in the e-text; other passages are cited by e-text page (p.1–p.4).
speaker: Maheśvara
